sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)

literature_notes: All four ledger lines were examined. L1/L2 describe a commercial Genscript pcDNA3.1+DYK plasmid (Clone OMu04791) carrying a FLAG tag in full-length Slc16a14; the tag position is never stated in the paper, which is the explicit disqualifying condition for commercial plasmids. L3/L4 describe C- or N-terminal Strep-HA / HA-Twin-Strep tags on SLC16A14. The computed topology places the N-terminus (residues 1–30) in the intracellular compartment and the C-terminus (residues 495–510) also intracellular; SLC16A14 is a 12-TM transporter with a cytoplasmic N-tail and cytoplasmic C-tail. Neither terminus is extracellular, so neither tag position qualifies as a surface tag site. No ledger line grounds an insertion in any extracellular loop. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: N-terminal Strep-HA tag reported on SLC16A14; topology places residues 1–30 in the intracellular compartment, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
C-terminal HA-Twin-Strep tag reported on SLC16A14; topology places residues 495–510 in the intracellular compartment, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
